question: Client assets per advisor across the five -- and is that comparison even valid?

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: Total Client Assets, defined as the sum of Wealth Management client assets and Investment Management AUM, reached $10.5 trillion as of September 30, 2026, per CFO Sharon Yeshaya (MS-TR-2026Q3#18). Total client assets grew by nearly $400 billion during 3Q26 to a record $10.5 trillion per CEO Edward Pick (MS-TR-2026Q3#2). Total client assets stood at $10 trillion as of June 30, 2026 (MS-TR-2026Q2#2; MS-TR-2026Q2#19). Total client assets exceeded $9 trillion as of March 31, 2026 (MS-TR-2026Q1#3). The Wealth and Investment Management businesses exited 2025 with $9.3 trillion in total client assets (MS-TR-2025Q4#25; MS-PR-2026-01-15-01#0; MS-TR-2025Q4#4).

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Total client assets were $13.33 trillion at September 30, 2026, up 15% year-over-year (SCHW-PR-2026-10-15-01#2), and $13.08 trillion at June 30, 2026, up 10% from year-end 2025 (SCHW-10Q-2026Q2#22). Total client assets ended 1Q26 at $11.77 trillion, down 1% from year-end 2025 (SCHW-10Q-2026Q1#19), and reached $11.90 trillion at December 31, 2025, up 18% on the year (SCHW-10K-2025#129).

Edward Jones: The Partnership ended fiscal year 2025 with $2.5 trillion in total client assets under care (AUC), including $1.1 trillion of advisory programs AUC (EDJ-10K-2025#131). Total client AUC was $2,306 billion at 2Q25 period end (EDJ-10Q-2025Q2#63), $2,421 billion at 3Q25 period end (EDJ-10Q-2025Q3#66), $2,417 billion at 1Q26 period end (EDJ-10Q-2026Q1#51), and $2,647 billion (about $2.6 trillion) at 2Q26 period end (EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#59; EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#61).

Merrill: Merrill Wealth Management reported $1.7 trillion in AUM balances at year-end 2025 (BAC-PR-2026-01-14-01#13), $1.7 trillion at March 31, 2026 (BAC-PR-2026-04-15-01#11), $1.8 trillion at June 30, 2026 (BAC-PR-2026-07-14-01#11), and $1.9 trillion at September 30, 2026 (BAC-PR-2026-10-14-01#12). The firm defines assets under management as managed assets under advisory and/or discretion of GWIM (BAC-SUPP-2026Q3#54).

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported client assets under administration of $1,571.1 billion (September 30, 2024), $1,557.5 billion (December 31, 2024), $1,535.9 billion (March 31, 2025), $1,637.1 billion (June 30, 2025), $1,730.6 billion (September 30, 2025), $1,773.1 billion (December 31, 2025), $1,762.9 billion (March 31, 2026), and $1,922.4 billion (June 30, 2026).
Morgan Stanley: reported 15,950 Wealth Management representatives as of December 31, 2020, 15,469 as of September 30, 2020, and 15,468 as of December 31, 2019 (MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1).

Edward Jones: reported 20,514 financial advisors (actual) at period end for 2Q26 (EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#60) and 20,309 at period end for 2Q25 (EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#60); averages were 20,537 for 2Q26 and 20,316 for 2Q25 (EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#60). At year end, financial advisors (actual) were 20,425 for 2025, 20,125 for 2024, and 19,232 for 2023, with averages of 20,331, 19,650, and 18,945 respectively (EDJ-10K-2025#130).

Raymond James Financial: For the whole firm (excluding RCS-division advisors), total financial advisors were 8,943 as of September 30, 2025 (a record, RJF-10K-2025#227; RJF-TR-2025Q3#4), 8,787 as of September 30, 2024, and 8,712 as of September 30, 2023 (RJF-10K-2025#227). Employee advisors were 3,878 (2025), 3,826 (2024), and 3,693 (2023); independent contractor advisors were 5,065 (2025), 4,961 (2024), and 5,019 (2023) (RJF-10K-2025#227). Separately, for the Private Client Group, Raymond James reported 8,731 PCG advisors as of approximately March 31, 2025 (RJF-DECK-2025-investor-day#30; RJF-DECK-2025-investor-day#43).

The comparison: The client assets per advisor figures across the five firms cannot be validly compared side by side, because the underlying client-asset measures and advisor-count measures differ by firm. Morgan Stanley's advisor count is labeled 'Wealth Management representatives' (15,950 at December 31, 2020, MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1), and its asset measure is Total Client Assets, the sum of Wealth Management client assets and Investment Management AUM (MS-DECK-2026-strategic-update#28). Schwab reports no financial-advisor headcount; it reports full-time-equivalent employees (approximately 33,000, SCHW-10K-2025#49) and, for Advisor Services, more than 16,000 independent advisory firms (SCHW-TR-2026Q3#10), with client assets that include custodial assets of independent RIAs (SCHW-10K-2025#26). Edward Jones counts 'financial advisors (actual)' (EDJ-10Q-2026Q1#51), many of whom are employees (EDJ-10K-2025#59), and measures 'assets under care' ($2.6 trillion in 2Q26, EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#61). Merrill's advisor count is 'Total wealth advisors' including advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking (18,916 at 2023Q4, BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2), which is broader than Merrill alone, and its AUM is defined as managed assets under advisory and/or discretion of GWIM (BAC-SUPP-2026Q3#54). Raymond James excludes RCS-division advisors from its financial advisor metric even though their client assets are included in AUA (RJF-10K-2025#228), and reports Private Client Group AUA of $1.67 trillion with 8,943 advisors as of September 30, 2025 (RJF-10K-2025#9). Because client-asset definitions (total client assets, total client assets under care, AUM, AUA), advisor-count definitions, and covered business scopes differ, and the per-advisor figures are not based on a common definition, the figures are not comparable.

adjacent.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab's Form ADV reports that approximately 4,127 of its employees perform investment advisory functions (including research) (SCHW-ADV1A-2026#1), approximately 6,584 are registered as investment adviser representatives (SCHW-ADV1A-2026#1), and approximately 30,690 total employees (SCHW-ADV1A-2026#1); as of December 31, 2025 Schwab had approximately 33,000 full-time-equivalent employees (SCHW-10K-2025#49).
adjacent.differs_because: No passage states a single 'advisor headcount' for the firm; the passages only give Form ADV regulatory counts and total/full-time employee counts, none of which equals the firm's own financial-consultant/wealth-advisor count.

adjacent.text: Merrill: Merrill's investor day deck reports more than 15,000 wealth advisors for Merrill combined with the Private Bank (BAC-DECK-2025-investor-day#9); at period end 2023Q4 the firm reported 18,916 total wealth advisors including advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2). Merrill's Form ADV reports approximately 26,599 employees who are registered representatives of a broker-dealer and approximately 32,960 total employees (MER-ADV1A-2026#1).
adjacent.differs_because: The passages report wealth advisors for wider units than Merrill alone (Merrill combined with the Private Bank, or all GWIM and Consumer Banking wealth businesses), and employee/registered-representative counts rather than Merrill's own advisor headcount.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: reported total Wealth Management client assets of $8,433 billion at September 30, 2026 (MS-SUPP-2026Q3#16) and $7,381 billion at December 31, 2025 (MS-SUPP-2025Q4#14); advisor-led client assets of $6,631 billion at September 30, 2026 (MS-SUPP-2026Q3#16) and $5,715 billion at December 31, 2025 (MS-10K-2025#166).
adjacent.differs_because: These are total and advisor-led client assets, not a computed or disclosed client-assets-per-advisor figure, and no current advisor count is disclosed to pair with them.

adjacent.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: reported total client assets of $13.08 trillion at June 30, 2026 alongside 39.8 million active brokerage accounts (SCHW-PR-2026-07-21-01#11); $13.33 trillion at September 30, 2026 (SCHW-PR-2026-10-15-01#2); $11.90 trillion at December 31, 2025 alongside 38.5 million active brokerage accounts (SCHW-PR-2026-01-21-01#9); and Advisor Services segment client assets of $5,845.9 billion at September 30, 2026 (SCHW-PR-2026-10-15-01#41).
adjacent.differs_because: These are client-asset figures and brokerage-account counts, not client assets per advisor, and Schwab does not report a financial-advisor headcount to divide by.

adjacent.text: Edward Jones: ended 2025 with $2.5 trillion in client AUC (numerator) and 20,425 financial advisors (denominator) (EDJ-10K-2025#131); ended 2Q25 with $2.3 trillion AUC and 20,309 financial advisors (EDJ-10Q-2025Q2#67); ended 2Q26 with $2.6 trillion AUC and 20,514 financial advisors (EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#53; EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#61); and ended 1Q26 with $2.4 trillion AUC and 20,550 financial advisors (EDJ-10Q-2026Q1#46; EDJ-10Q-2026Q1#52).
adjacent.differs_because: These provide the numerator and denominator for client assets per advisor but the ratio itself is not disclosed; any ratio would be code-computed and unverified.

adjacent.text: Merrill: Merrill Wealth Management reported client balances of $3,992,312 million at December 31, 2025 (BAC-SUPP-2025Q4#56) and $4,240,601 million at September 30, 2026 (BAC-SUPP-2026Q3#53). Total GWIM client balances were $5,056,787 million at September 30, 2026 (BAC-SUPP-2026Q3#54). Total wealth advisors were 18,916 at December 31, 2023 (and 19,273 at December 31, 2022), including advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking (BAC-SUPP-2023Q4#2).
adjacent.differs_because: These are client balances and a wider advisor count (GWIM and Consumer Banking), not a Merrill-only client-assets-per-advisor figure.

adjacent.text: Raymond James Financial: reported total Private Client Group AUA of $1.67 trillion (of which $1.01 trillion in fee-based accounts) and 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2025 (RJF-10K-2025#9); total advisors were 8,943 (3,878 employees and 5,065 independent contractors) at September 30, 2025, versus 8,787 in 2024 and 8,712 in 2023 (RJF-10K-2025#227); RCS AUA totaled $217.3 billion as of September 30, 2025 (RJF-10K-2025#12); and the Financial Institutions Division reports $166 million in average AUM per advisor across 940 advisors at 160 financial institutions (RJF-PR-web-bank-and-credit-union-advisors#0).
adjacent.differs_because: The $166 million figure is the Financial Institutions Division's disclosed average AUM per advisor, not a firm-wide client-assets-per-advisor figure; the rest are numerator/denominator components.
